subject: Conversion of raw GGIR epoch data to 60 second epoch data

messages.author: 8b544cbd8df3ddb3
messages.subject: Conversion of raw GGIR epoch data to 60 second epoch data
parts:
Hello,

        Our research group wants to compare wrist-worn accelerometer data from Actilife using 60 second epochs, and GGIR raw epoch data (which uses 5 second epochs). 

        Is one reasonable way to do this by:
1) Getting output from the  "epochvalues2csv" function
2)  Averaging all the ENMO values within a particular minute to get the ENMO value for 60 second epochs (average ENMO of 12 five second epochs).
3) Apply ENMO cutpoints (Hildebrand) to get activity classifications for each epoch. 
4) Calculate how often the activity classifications differ between Actilife and GGIR across 60 second epochs.

        Thanks in advance,
        Raymond

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Conversion of raw GGIR epoch data to 60 second epoch data
parts:
Hi Raymond,

Sorry for the slow reply.

Note that GGIR allows you to specify epoch length with argument windowsizes.

The comparison you propose is not comparison between ActiLife and GGIR, but a comparison between ActiLife and the specific threshold proposed by Hildebrand and not GGIR as software tool that facilitates much more than just the Hildebrand threshold.

Thanks,
Vincent


Dr. Vincent van Hees
Independent consultant
